q: Should I use a hot water generator instead of a steam boiler for low-temperature heat?
title: Hot water generator vs steam boiler
short: If your process needs water below about 90 °C, making steam and then cooling it back to hot water wastes fuel through flash, condensate and blowdown losses. A hot water generator heats water directly. Check your process temperatures first, then compare fuel per kilolitre heated.
audience: Food, dairy, textile and pharma plants

ul: Flash steam and condensate not returned.
Trap and line losses at higher temperature.
Processes above water's boiling point, sterilisation or direct steam injection.
Sites where one boiler already serves high-temperature users.

p: Fuel per kilolitre of water heated, before and after, from invoices or a meter. A heat pump may beat both for low temperatures; see the linked page.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
